reading.body:
Alexandria Paolozzi Moore is named on 6 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm, for one client, FDD ACTION, and those filings name 15 separate bills.

The concentration is the pattern. Six filings, one firm, one client. A lobbying record this narrow describes a single engagement rather than a broad practice, and the 15 bills are the legislative surface that engagement touched, not 15 separate campaigns. The bills are identified only by number, so the data does not say what any of them would do or whether they concern data centers, interconnection, or electricity at all.

The disclosed prior government position is an internship in a House office in 2010. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires covered positions from the prior twenty years to be listed, so its presence is a disclosure requirement being met, not evidence of influence. Nothing here measures whether the lobbying succeeded, how much was spent, or what positions were advocated.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. It gives no spending figures, no agency contacts, no committee assignments, and no text of the bills. It also flags that a different lobbyist shares this name and has a separate record, so any count of AI lobbying activity should not merge the two.
